blocks.text: Evening on a Colombo roadside. KASUN pours tea at his small three-wheeler stall. ANUDI'S FATHER arrives and stands, looking over the stall.
The father looks at the cups, the kettle, the worn stool.
මේක මගේ දුව හුරු තැන නෙවෙයි.
blocks.speaker: Father

blocks.text: Kasun sets down the kettle. He does not answer at once.
ඒක මම දන්නවා. ඒත් මම මේක වෙනස් කරනවා.
blocks.speaker: Kasun

blocks.text: The father looks at him a long moment, then turns and walks to his car.

treatment.logline: On a warm Colombo evening, a tea-seller meets his lover’s father’s class test, absorbs the cut, and answers with a quiet promise as the father turns away.

arc.beat: He arrives to measure the man
arc.feeling: A polite test under streetlights; two worlds across a counter
The stall is appraised and dismissed; the words sting

treatment.approach: Street is character. Open wide and grounded, then climb steadily into faces. Lenses: 24mm/28mm for world and geography, 35mm/50mm for across-the-counter dialogue, 85mm for intimate singles, 100mm macro for steam, cups and kettle. Movement is restrained and motivated: locked-off or a slow push on key turns; little handheld drift for POV details; a sideways pan to follow the father’s exit. Foreground steam and counter edges layer depth; reflections and headlight bokeh carry the city. Play big lines on the listener’s face; push closest on the promise.

treatment.geography: The three-wheeler stall is parked curbside camera-right; its open counter faces camera-left toward the pavement and street. The father’s car is parked further camera-left along the curb. The line runs along the counter (Kasun inside, the father outside). We keep the camera on the stall/Kasun side of the line throughout, so Kasun reads frame-right facing left, the father frame-left facing right. The father arrives from the car at camera-left to the counter (b0), stays at the counter for the exchange, then exits back toward camera-left along the curb to the car (b7). The exit is followed with a pan that stays on our side of the line.
treatment.key_image: Amber steam billowing up from a dented kettle between two faces across a narrow counter, headlight bokeh drifting through.
advice: We chose to play L4 and L1 on Kasun’s face. If you prefer to see the father say those lines, we can swap shots 10 and 4 to on-speaker coverage.
We avoid readable phone or signage text and a detailed car door action; if you need a door close clearly seen, we’ll stage it out of frame and play it as sound.
If the father should be chauffeur-driven or arrive with others, that changes staging and must be written in the scene.
